scope: Proposition 3.12 (The current trajectory forced by nonflaring) of the manuscript “Baumslag-Solitar-free one-relator groups are hyperbolic” (preprints/Baumslag-Solitar-free-one-relator-groups-are-hyperbolic-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 258 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b578833682141115), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the hypotheses of Theo- rem 3.1, if G is not hyperbolic, there exist currents µs ∈ Curr(P) for s ∈ Z, signs ϵs ∈ {+, −}, and transition types τs with signs (ϵs, ϵs+1), such that (i) ∥µ0∥ = 1, every µs is nonzero, and sups∈Z ∥µs∥ < ∞; (ii) for every s there is a current νs ∈ Curr(Kτs ) with µs = (θτs,0)∗νs, µs+1 = (θτs,1)∗νs; (iii) all types are essential: any reversing type uses a double coset outside the common side subgroup. The constants in (3.14) apply to this trajectory. In particular, ∥µs∥ ≥ C−|s| for all s.
